ae.file: File:Flag of the United Arab Emirates.svg
ae.attribution: Public domain — Abdulla Mohammed Al Maainah (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the United Arab Emirates.svg)
ae.story: Designed by 19-year-old Abdullah Mohammed Al Maainah and adopted on 2 December 1971; red, green, white and black are the pan-Arab colours.
ae.altText: Red vertical band at the hoist, with green, white and black horizontal bands stretching to the right.

ar.attribution: Public domain — Manuel Belgrano (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Argentina.svg)
ar.story: Created by Manuel Belgrano and first raised in Rosario on 27 February 1812; the golden Sun of May was added in the centre in 1818.
ar.altText: Sky-blue, white and sky-blue horizontal bands with a golden sun with a face in the centre.

at.attribution: Public domain — Bundesministerium für Landesverteidigung (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Austria.svg)
at.story: Red, white and red in three equal bands — Austria's triband became its national flag again in 1919 and once more in 1945.
at.altText: Three horizontal bands: red, white and red.

au.attribution: Public domain — Unknown  (Vector graphics image by Ian Fieggen) (only minor code changes by uploader.) (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Australia (converted).svg)
au.story: Born of a 1901 design contest: the Union Jack, the seven-point Commonwealth Star and the Southern Cross stars on a blue field.
au.altText: Blue flag with the Union Jack in the top-left corner, a large white seven-pointed star below it and five white Southern Cross stars on the right.

bd.attribution: Public domain — See File history below for details. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Bangladesh.svg)
bd.story: Adopted on 17 January 1972: green for Bangladesh's lush land and a red disc, like the rising sun, for the sacrifice of the Liberation War.
bd.altText: Dark green flag with a large red circle slightly left of centre.

bg.attribution: Public domain; SVG by SKopp via Wikimedia Commons
bg.story: Bulgaria's white-green-red flag was first adopted after the 1877-78 war for independence and was restored by the 1991 constitution.
bg.altText: Three equal horizontal stripes: white, green, red.

br.attribution: Public domain — Raimundo Teixeira Mendes (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Brazil.svg)
br.story: Adopted on 19 November 1889: a blue globe of stars and the motto Ordem e Progresso inside a yellow diamond on a green field.
br.altText: Green flag with a yellow diamond in the middle holding a blue globe of white stars crossed by a white motto band.

ca.attribution: Public domain — via Wikimedia Commons (File:Flag of Canada (Pantone).svg)
ca.story: Proclaimed Canada's national flag in 1965: one red 11-point maple leaf in a white square between two red bands — the Maple Leaf.
ca.altText: Red, white and red vertical bands with a red 11-point maple leaf in the white centre.

cl.attribution: Public domain — See file history below for details. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Chile.svg)
cl.story: Adopted on 18 October 1817 and nicknamed La Estrella Solitaria, the Lone Star, for the white star in its blue corner.
cl.altText: White band over a red band, with a blue square in the top-left corner holding a white star.

cn.file: File:Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg
cn.attribution: Public domain — Zeng Liansong (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg)
cn.story: Adopted in 1949: one large gold star and four smaller gold stars on red, standing for the party and the people united.
cn.altText: Red flag with one large gold star and four smaller gold stars in the top-left corner.

co.attribution: Public domain; SVG via Wikimedia Commons
co.story: Colombia's wide yellow band takes up half the flag; its yellow-blue-red stripes took today's arrangement in 1861.
co.altText: A wide yellow top stripe over thinner blue and red horizontal stripes.

cu.attribution: Public domain — Miguel Teurbe Tolón and Narciso López (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Cuba.svg)
cu.story: Designed in 1849 and adopted on 20 May 1902: the Lone Star flag's red triangle holds one white star beside blue-white stripes.
cu.altText: Blue and white horizontal stripes with a red triangle at the left holding a white star.

cz.attribution: Public domain — Jaroslav Kursa (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the Czech Republic.svg)
cz.story: Czechia kept Czechoslovakia's flag at the 1993 split: white over red, with a blue triangle added in 1920 to differ from Poland.
cz.altText: White band over a red band, with a blue triangle reaching in from the left side.

de.attribution: Public domain — User:SKopp, User:Madden, and other users (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Germany.svg)
de.story: Black, red and gold: first flown in 1848, Germany's tricolour became the national flag in 1919 and returned in 1949.
de.altText: Three horizontal bands: black, red and gold.

dk.attribution: Public domain — Madden and others (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Denmark.svg)
dk.story: The Dannebrog: a red flag whose white Nordic cross reaches every edge and sits shifted toward the hoist.
dk.altText: Red flag with a white cross reaching all four edges, shifted toward the left.

dz.attribution: Public domain — Original: National Liberation Front of Algeria Vector: SKopp (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Algeria.svg)
dz.story: Adopted on 3 July 1962: green and white bands with a red star and crescent in the centre, a symbol of Islam.
dz.altText: Green and white vertical halves with a red crescent and a red star in the centre.

ee.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Original: Unknown author Vector: SKopp , PeepP and ‍others via Wikimedia Commons
ee.story: Estonia's blue-black-white flag became the national flag in 1918, was banned under Soviet rule, and flew freely again from 1988.
ee.altText: Three equal horizontal stripes: blue, black, white.

eg.attribution: Public domain — See File history below for details. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Egypt.svg)
eg.story: Red, white and black bands from the 1952 revolution's Arab Liberation Flag, with the golden Eagle of Saladin in the centre.
eg.altText: Red, white and black horizontal bands with a golden eagle in the centre of the white band.

et.attribution: Public domain — Drawn by User:SKopp (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Ethiopia.svg)
et.story: Green, yellow and red held meaning since the 1600s; the modern tricolour dates to 1897 and today's emblem flag to 1996.
et.altText: Green, yellow and red horizontal bands with a blue disc and gold emblem in the centre.

fi.attribution: Public domain — Unknown (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Finland.svg)
fi.story: The siniristilippu, the blue-cross flag, was adopted just after Finland became independent from Russia in the early 1900s.
fi.altText: White flag with a blue cross reaching all four edges, shifted toward the left.

fr.attribution: Public domain — Original: Unknown Vector:  SKopp (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of France.svg)
fr.story: Born in the French Revolution: three vertical bands of blue, white and red — a tricolour copied by flags around the world.
fr.altText: Three vertical bands: blue, white and red.

gb.attribution: Public domain — Original: Acts of Union 1800 Vector:  Yaddah (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the United Kingdom (3-5).svg)
gb.story: The Union Jack layers the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland on blue; today's combined form dates to 1801.
gb.altText: Blue flag layered with red and white straight and diagonal crosses — the Union Jack.

gh.attribution: Public domain — Theodosia Okoh (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Ghana.svg)
gh.story: Designed by Theodosia Okoh for independence in 1957: red, gold and green with the Black Star of African freedom in the centre.
gh.altText: Red, gold and green horizontal bands with a large black star in the centre.

gr.attribution: Public domain — Unknown authorUnknown author (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Greece.svg)
gr.story: Adopted on 13 January 1822: nine blue-and-white stripes and a white cross in the corner, the cross standing for Christianity.
gr.altText: Nine blue-and-white horizontal stripes with a blue square in the top-left corner holding a white cross.

hu.attribution: Public domain — SKopp (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Hungary.svg)
hu.story: Red-white-green has been Hungary's official flag in this exact form since 23 May 1957; its colours reach back to the Middle Ages.
hu.altText: Three horizontal bands: red, white and green.

id.attribution: Public domain — Jayakatwang (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Indonesia.svg)
id.story: The Sang Saka Merah Putih, the heirloom red-and-white, was first hoisted at Indonesia's independence proclamation on 17 August 1945.
id.altText: Two horizontal bands: red on top and white below.

ie.attribution: Public domain — Éire (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Ireland.svg)
ie.story: Green, white and orange: the white middle of Ireland's tricolour stands for peace between the traditions the other bands represent.
ie.altText: Three vertical bands: green, white and orange.

in.attribution: Public domain — Government of India (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of India.svg)
in.story: Adopted on 15 August 1947: saffron, white and green, with the navy-blue Ashoka Chakra — a 24-spoke wheel — in the centre.
in.altText: Saffron, white and green horizontal bands with a navy-blue 24-spoke wheel in the centre.

iq.attribution: Public domain; SVG via Wikimedia Commons
iq.story: Iraq's red-white-black flag, in its current form since 2008, carries the takbir - 'God is greatest' - in green Kufic script.
iq.altText: Red, white and black horizontal stripes with green Arabic writing across the white stripe.

ir.attribution: Public domain; SVG by SVG file: SiBr 4 Designer: Hamid Nadimi Construction: ISIRI via Wikimedia Commons
ir.story: Iran's green-white-red flag took its current form in 1980; its centre emblem builds the word 'Allah' from four crescents and a sword.
ir.altText: Green, white and red horizontal stripes with a red emblem in the centre and white script along the inner stripe edges.

is.attribution: Public domain — Original: Matthías Þórðarson Vector:  Árni Dagur and Magasjukur2 (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Iceland.svg)
is.story: Set by law on 17 June 1944, the day Iceland became a republic: a white cross on sky blue with a fiery-red cross inside it.
is.altText: Blue flag with a white cross reaching the edges and a thinner red cross inside it.

it.attribution: Public domain — See below. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Italy.svg)
it.story: Green, white and red vertical bands — Italy's Tricolour is written into Article 12 of the Italian Constitution.
it.altText: Three vertical bands: green, white and red.

jp.attribution: Public domain — Various (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Japan.svg)
jp.story: The Hinomaru, a red sun disc on white, stands for Japan's nickname: the Land of the Rising Sun.
jp.altText: White flag with a red circle in the centre.

kr.attribution: Public domain — Original: Government of the Republic of Korea Vector:  Great Brightstar and others (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of South Korea.svg)
kr.story: The Taegeukgi, adopted by South Korea in 1948: a red-and-blue taegeuk for balance, with a black trigram in each corner.
kr.altText: White flag with a red-and-blue swirl circle in the centre and black trigram marks in the four corners.

ma.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Denelson83 , Zscout370 via Wikimedia Commons
ma.story: Morocco's flag has flown since 1915: a green five-pointed star, standing for the five pillars of Islam, centred on a red field.
ma.altText: Plain red flag with a green five-pointed star outline in the centre.

ng.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Jon Harald Søby . via Wikimedia Commons
ng.story: Designed by Taiwo Akinkunmi, Nigeria's flag flew first at independence in 1960; green is for farming, white for peace and unity.
ng.altText: Three equal vertical stripes: green, white, green.

nl.attribution: Public domain — Zscout370 (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the Netherlands.svg)
nl.story: The world's oldest tricolour still in use: red, white and blue that grew from the 1500s orange-white-blue Prince's Flag.
nl.altText: Three horizontal bands: red, white and blue.

no.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Original: Fredrik Meltzer Vector: Gutten på Hemsen via Wikimedia Commons
no.story: Norway's red flag has a blue cross outlined in white; crosses reaching the edges are a tradition shared by its Nordic neighbours.
no.altText: Red flag with a white-outlined navy blue cross reaching the edges, shifted toward the pole.

np.attribution: Public domain — Drawn by Pumbaa80, Achim1999 (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Nepal.svg)
np.story: The world's only non-rectangular national flag: two stacked pennants, red for bravery and a blue border for peace.
np.altText: A red double-pennant flag, taller than wide, edged in blue with a white crescent moon above and a white sun below.

nz.attribution: Public domain — Original: Albert Hastings Markham Vector:  Zscout370, Hugh Jass, s. File history (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of New Zealand.svg)
nz.story: A blue ensign with the Union Jack in the corner and four red stars, rimmed in white, tracing the Southern Cross.
nz.altText: Blue flag with the Union Jack in the top-left corner and four red stars with white rims on the right.

pe.attribution: Public domain — David Benbennick (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Peru.svg)
pe.story: Adopted by Congress on 25 February 1825: red-white-red vertical bands, nicknamed the Bicolour; Flag Day is 7 June.
pe.altText: Three vertical bands: red, white and red.

ph.attribution: Public domain — See File history below for details. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the Philippines.svg)
ph.story: Three Stars and a Sun: the golden sun's eight rays recall the first eight provinces that rose against Spain in 1896.
ph.altText: Blue band over a red band, with a white triangle at the left holding a gold sun and three gold stars.

pl.attribution: Public domain — See below. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Poland.svg)
pl.story: White over red are Poland's national colours, set in its constitution; the plain bicolour is the everyday national flag.
pl.altText: Two horizontal bands: white on top and red below.

pt.attribution: Public domain — via Wikimedia Commons (File:Flag of Portugal.svg)
pt.story: Announced in 1910 after the republican revolution: green and red split the field, with armillary sphere and shield at the join.
pt.altText: A green band at the left and a larger red field, with a yellow armillary sphere and a red-and-white shield where they meet.

ro.attribution: Public domain; SVG by AdiJapan via Wikimedia Commons
ro.story: Romania's blue-yellow-red vertical stripes took their current form in 1989, in the wake of the Romanian Revolution.
ro.altText: Three equal vertical stripes: blue, yellow, red.

ru.attribution: Public domain — Peter the Great (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Russia.svg)
ru.story: Three equal horizontal bands — white on top, blue in the middle and red at the bottom — make up Russia's tricolour.
ru.altText: Three horizontal bands: white, blue and red.

se.attribution: Public domain — Jon Harald Søby and others. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Sweden.svg)
se.story: A gold Nordic cross on light blue: Sweden's colours come from its 1442 coat of arms, blue quarters divided by a golden cross.
se.altText: Light blue flag with a yellow cross reaching all four edges, shifted toward the left.

sg.attribution: Public domain — Original: Government of Singapore Vector:  Zscout370 (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Singapore.svg)
sg.story: Adopted in 1959, designed under Toh Chin Chye: red over white with a crescent and five stars for a young nation on the rise.
sg.altText: Red band over a white band, with a white crescent moon and five small white stars in the top-left corner.

th.attribution: Public domain — Zscout370 (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Thailand.svg)
th.story: Adopted by royal decree of Rama VI on 28 September 1917: red, white, blue, white and red stripes, the blue one double-width.
th.altText: Five horizontal stripes: red, white, blue (double width), white and red.

tn.attribution: Public domain — Various Wikimedia Commons' contributors (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Tunisia.svg)
tn.story: Created after the Battle of Navarino on 20 October 1827 by Hussein II: a red flag with a white disc holding a red crescent and star, clarified by law in 1999.
tn.altText: Red flag with a white circle in the centre holding a red crescent and a red five-pointed star.

ua.attribution: Public domain — Government of Ukraine (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Ukraine.svg)
ua.story: Two equally sized horizontal bands — blue on top and yellow below — make up Ukraine's national flag.
ua.altText: Two horizontal bands: blue on top and yellow below.

us.attribution: Public domain — Uploaded by Dbenbenn; edited by users such as Zscout370, Jacobolus, Indolences, and Technion. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of the United States.svg)
us.story: Thirteen red-and-white stripes for the first colonies, and fifty white stars on blue — one for each U.S. state today.
us.altText: Thirteen red-and-white stripes with a blue rectangle in the top-left corner holding fifty small white stars.

us-ak.attribution: Benny Benson — It is an edited form of a file from openclipart.org , specifically usa_alaska.svg .
us-ak.story: Benny Benson's 1927 contest-winning design shows the Big Dipper and the North Star in gold on Alaska's dark blue.
us-ak.altText: Dark blue flag with eight gold stars: seven forming the Big Dipper saucepan shape and one larger North Star at the top right.

us-al.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Steve Hall via Wikimedia Commons
us-al.story: Alabama's flag, adopted in 1895, is a crimson diagonal cross of St Andrew on white, designed by lawmaker John W. A. Sanford Jr.
us-al.altText: White flag with a crimson red diagonal cross running from corner to corner.

us-ar.attribution: Public domain file on Wikimedia Commons
us-ar.story: Arkansas's red flag holds a white diamond with 29 stars: 25 small white ones in its blue border and four blue ones inside.
us-ar.altText: Red flag with a large white diamond edged in blue with 25 white stars, the word Arkansas and four blue stars inside the diamond.

us-az.story: Arizona's flag fans 13 red-and-gold rays for the first 13 colonies, with a copper star for its copper at the centre.
us-az.altText: Top half of red and gold sun rays fanning out, blue bottom half, and a large copper-coloured star in the centre.

us-co.attribution: Original: Andrew Carlyle Carson Vector: Fleminra — Own work based on: Colorado State Flag – 50states . 50states.com . Retrieved on 2025-04-14 .
us-co.story: Adopted in 1911, Colorado's flag means: blue for sky, white for snowy peaks, gold for sunshine, red for ruddy earth.
us-co.altText: Blue, white and blue horizontal stripes with a big red letter C filled with a gold disc.

us-hi.attribution: Dbenbenn — This SVG flag includes elements that have been taken or adapted from this flag:
us-hi.story: Used since 1845, Hawaii's flag pairs eight stripes with Britain's Union Jack, a legacy of its Royal Navy ties.
us-hi.altText: Eight white, red and blue horizontal stripes with Britain's Union Jack in the top-left corner.

us-in.attribution: The Indiana state flag was designed by Paul Hadley in 1917. This SVG file was made by Zscout370 with some modifications by HoosierMan1816 . — [1] [2]
us-in.story: Adopted in 1917, Indiana's flag rings a gold torch with 19 stars; the biggest, above the flame, is Indiana itself.
us-in.altText: Dark blue flag with a gold flaming torch in the centre ringed by 19 gold stars and rays, with the word Indiana above.

us-md.story: Adopted in 1904, Maryland's flag uses Lord Baltimore's 17th-century arms: black-and-gold checks beside red-and-white crosses.
us-md.altText: Flag split into quarters of black-and-gold checks and red-and-white crosses with small cross shapes at the corners.

us-mn.attribution: Original: Minnesota State Emblems Redesign Commission Vector: Jamie Eilat , Undertiago — Own work based on: The New Official Flag and Great Seal — Report of the Minnesota State Emblems Redesign Commission to the Minnesota Legislature and Governor
us-mn.story: New in 2024! Minnesota's flag shows an eight-point North Star on a dark-blue shape of the state, beside light-blue waters.
us-mn.altText: Dark blue shape like Minnesota on the left with a white eight-pointed star, beside a plain light blue field.

us-nm.attribution: Public domain file on Wikimedia Commons
us-nm.story: Adopted in 1925, New Mexico's gold flag carries the red Zia sun, a sacred symbol of the Zia people.
us-nm.altText: Bright yellow flag with a red Zia sun symbol in the centre: a circle with four groups of four rays.

us-oh.attribution: John Eisenmann — Own work based on: The Ohio State Flag (design).jpg and US D34810 S.pdf and http://www.sos.state.oh.us/sos/upload/publications/agency/flag-110.pdf
us-oh.story: Designed in 1901 and adopted in 1902, Ohio's swallowtail flag has a big disc that hints at the letter O.
us-oh.altText: Swallowtail flag with red and white stripes, a blue triangle at the hoist with 17 white stars and a large red-and-white disc like the letter O.

us-ri.attribution: Public domain; SVG by Xrmap flag collection 2.7 via Wikimedia Commons
us-ri.story: Rhode Island's white flag rings a gold anchor - a symbol of hope - with 13 gold stars for the original Thirteen Colonies.
us-ri.altText: White flag with a gold anchor in the centre, ringed by 13 gold stars, above a blue ribbon reading HOPE.

us-tn.attribution: -xfi- — Based on tnmilitary.org ( original ) and crwflags.com ( original )
us-tn.story: Tennessee's red flag ends in a blue bar and centres three white stars on a blue circle ringed in white.
us-tn.altText: Red flag with a thin white line and a blue bar at the far edge, and a blue circle ringed in white with three white stars in the centre.

us-tx.story: Texas's Lone Star flag is one of only two state flags that first served as the flag of an independent country.
us-tx.altText: Blue vertical band with one white star, beside white and red horizontal bands — the Lone Star flag.

us-ut.attribution: The State of Utah — Utah Department of Cultural & Community Engagement: https://flag.utah.gov/content/ (from the SVG in "download graphic package")
us-ut.story: New in 2024! Utah's flag puts a gold beehive, for industry, in a blue hexagon over white mountains and red rock.
us-ut.altText: Blue top band, white middle band shaped like mountain peaks, and red bottom band, with a blue hexagon holding a gold beehive and a white star.

vn.attribution: Public domain — See File history below for details. (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of Vietnam.svg)
vn.story: Designed in 1940: a gold star on red whose five points stand for intellectuals, farmers, workers, entrepreneurs and soldiers.
vn.altText: Red flag with one large gold five-pointed star in the centre.

za.attribution: Public domain — Flag design by Frederick Brownell, image by Wikimedia Commons users (via Wikimedia Commons, File:Flag of South Africa.svg)
za.story: Designed in March 1994 and adopted on 27 April 1994 for South Africa's first democratic election, replacing the 1928 flag.
za.altText: A green Y-shape lying on its side divides red at the top from blue at the bottom, edged in gold and white, with a black triangle at the left.
